evidence_they_had_already_seen.note: 3 of 3 live theories are scored only on measurements that already existed when they were stated. That is not a fault by itself — a principle stated in round 6 has to explain rounds 1 to 5, and this is how it earns its way in. It is a different claim once a theory has met NO measurement made after it was written: nothing it said could have come out wrong. The measurement that would settle this for `修复 Yoshida 权重后 SYM4 恢复四阶收敛与保辛性，浏览器自检 19` is one candidate it has not already seen: build a row that varies whatever it names and record it. If the theory holds there, it stops being a re-reading of what was already on the shelf.

bare_leader.label: selftest_ms
bare_leader.note: `selftest_ms` is the best candidate this campaign has and the record holds nothing it can generate variants of — no formula, no program, no holes, just a label and a number. Every generator here works from a representation, so none of them can move toward it. If you know what it does, record it: `form` when it is an expression, `program` for source when it has a loop, a state or a fixed point, or `program` plus `holes` when the skeleton is fixed and only its components are worth searching. Any of the three opens a generator that can search toward it. Left as a bare label it stays a number you can be beaten by and cannot chase.

snapshot.program_countdown:
0 of the scored candidates carry a `program`. At 5 this stops enumerating \
             and returns a breeding set instead — the best programs so far, the worst for \
             contrast, and the factors on which the two groups differ, which is the material for \
             writing a better one. 5 more to go. A `program` is a free-text field, not a source dump: the ones already recorded \
                 in this project run a median of 80 characters — `per-gene \
                 RidgeCV(alphas=[0.1,1,10,100], cv=3) on features f0..f7` is one of them. That is \
                 less than these candidates already spend on `factors`. It needs no `n_features`, \
                 no numeric columns and no grammar: unlike `form`, which cannot be generated \
                 until the campaign declares how many columns a formula may read, a program is \
                 source text and the record derives what it can from it as written.
